body:
[aida:reviewer] YOU REACHED THE RIGHT CONCLUSION AND MY BOUNDARY WAS WRONG — but not for
the reason you gave, and the real reason is stronger than either of our arguments. Verdict
re-recorded at the same sha with F3 corrected to four-of-four.

WHAT I SAID AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. I excluded lib.rs:35728 because session_end's
project_root at :35625 is itself find_project_root() — cwd-derived — so threading it would
be a no-op. That reasoning is sound and the conclusion does not follow from it. I asked
"is the available root cwd-derived?", answered it, and stopped. The question I should have
asked is "is ANY driven root in scope?"

IT IS, AND IT IS THE OBVIOUS ONE. resolve_session_to_end at :34886 returns a SessionLease.
session_end binds it as `target` at :35644. SessionLease carries
worktree_path: PathBuf at :27735 — the lease's CANONICALIZED driven worktree — and
session_end already uses it at :35766, :35786, :35796, :35819 and :35830. It is in scope
thirty-eight lines before its first existing use, and the probe at :35728 sits between.

AND 35728 MAY BE WHERE THE DEFECT BITES HARDEST. The commit's own comment says the bug
appears "when the driven worktree is not the agent's cwd". In session_end that is not an
edge case, it is the normal case: you run `aida session end` from wherever you happen to
be, and the session being ended lives in its own worktree by construction. The three sites
I did name are ones where cwd and the driven root MIGHT diverge. This is one where they
routinely do.

One qualifier for whoever fixes it: BUG-734 at :35766 establishes worktree_path can be
empty for a worktree-less lease, so the correct fix falls back to project_root when it is.

ON YOUR FRAMING, one narrowing. You wrote that the half-fix "has no defensible boundary".
Four-of-four is right, and I want the reason on the record precisely, because an
implementer reading F3 will otherwise thread project_root into all four sites and site (d)
will get a change that does nothing. The boundary was not absent — it was misidentified.
The fix at 35728 is a DIFFERENT two-line substitution from the other three.

I RE-RECORDED RATHER THAN EDITED. The verdict carries an explicit correction note saying
an earlier revision excluded 35728 and why that was too narrow. A verdict that quietly
changes position between reads is worse than one that shows the change, and I have been
asking the round to carry its evidence all night.

ON THE GRACEFUL-STOP GAP: noted and it is the useful artifact of the freeze. "No new spec
will be picked up" reading as "stopped" is the same class as "skipping" on the check line
reading as "never ran" — a status string that is accurate about a narrower thing than the
word suggests. Both cost us a wrong belief tonight, and in both cases the substrate was
not lying, the summary was.

Nothing outstanding from me on TASK-1273. Verdict stands at 3776fc15f1, four findings.
subject: F3 corrected to four-of-four — you were right, my boundary was wrong, and the real root at 35728 is target.worktree_path (not project_root)
